A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chrono point-tracking work. All 11 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and end matter, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Chrono tracking results, architectural ablations, efficiency measurements, and experiments integrating Chrono with LocoTrack in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds backbone comparisons, RGB-Stacking results, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Equation (3) changes the stated attention computation by dividing query-key dot products by sqrt(dk). This is a limited revision to the specified operation; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed. The backbone, adapter structure, prediction procedure, loss, and optional LocoTrack integration otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kubric Panning-MOVi-E for training and evaluate DAVIS, Kinetics, and RGB-Stacking. RGB-Stacking already appears in v1 Table 4. Its expanded backbone-only evaluation in v2 changes model configurations and reported results within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the pretrained CoTracker backbone to the direct backbone comparisons in Tables 1 and 2. CoTracker's complete tracking pipeline already appeared in Table 4, but this backbone comparator is new to those experiments. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 extends backbone-only RGB-Stacking evaluation to both strided and first-query protocols and adds additional-parameter counts and GPU-memory measurements in Tables 3 and 7. Existing training budgets, position-accuracy thresholds, query-mode definitions, and throughput hardware remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The resource-overhead analysis now examines memory consumption and additional parameters, extending the earlier latency and refiner-parameter comparisons. Temporal-aggregation and adapter-placement ablations, the LocoTrack integration analysis, and PCA visualizations retain their existing evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its results. Averaging position accuracy across thresholds is retained and does not constitute run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 substantially expand direct backbone results with RGB-Stacking and CoTracker comparisons. Chrono-S/B newly report RGB-Stacking averages of 84.3/86.0 in strided mode and 80.2/82.1 in first-query mode. Resource results are also added, while matched existing scores remain unchanged. One new result is internally inconsistent: CoTracker's Kinetics-strided average is reported as 58.2, although its five displayed threshold scores average to 51.6.

T1.justification: Equation (3) revises the mathematical definition of temporal-attention weights by introducing sqrt(dk) scaling in both numerator and denominator. This changes the defined weights rather than merely their notation. Other mathematical definitions and equations are retained; neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims about temporally aware DINOv2 features enabling accurate, efficient tracking with reduced dependence on refinement. v2 highlights optional refinement in the introduction, but that capability and its supporting experiment already appear in v1 Section 4.4 and Table 4.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits the standalone method's focus to position prediction rather than occlusion prediction in Section 3.1. Section 4.3 also qualifies superiority from all thresholds to most thresholds and average accuracy, consistent with exceptions in the expanded comparisons.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports additional-parameter counts of 16.2M and 26.0M for Chrono-S/B and GPU-memory usage of 1,550 and 2,998 MiB. It also documents RGB-Stacking's 50-video size and content. Existing optimization settings, hardware disclosures, adapter hyperparameters, and project-page access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Beyond pick-and-place: Tackling robotic stacking of diverse shapes and Attention is all you need, supporting the dataset description and attention scaling. Existing references and the paper's positioning around temporally aware feature backbones are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Localized revisions update the introduction, task-scope explanation, dataset description, results discussion, and efficiency subsection. v2 also adds acknowledgements. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a new pipeline-comparison Figure 1 and relocates the original opening visualization to Figure 2. It revises the architecture illustration, expands Tables 1-3 and 7, introduces best/second-best markings, compresses Table 4 from full width to one column, and relocates the retained PCA figure. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The expanded backbone comparisons and explicit parameter and memory costs strengthen empirical support and clarify efficiency tradeoffs. The position-only scope statement and qualification to most thresholds improve precision. These are limited gains to an otherwise stable study; the inconsistent new CoTracker Kinetics-strided average in Table 1 weakens confidence in that particular comparison.
